{{Short description|Shorthand notation in the algebra}}
'''Plethystic substitution''' is a shorthand notation for a common kind of substitution in the [[Ring of symmetric functions|algebra of symmetric functions]] and that of [[Symmetric polynomial|symmetric polynomials]].  It is essentially basic substitution of variables, but allows for a change in the number of variables used.

==Definition==

The formal definition of plethystic substitution relies on the fact that the ring of symmetric functions <math>\Lambda_R(x_1,x_2,\ldots)</math> is generated as an ''R''-algebra by the power sum symmetric functions

: <math>p_k=x_1^k+x_2^k+x_3^k+\cdots.</math>

For any symmetric function <math>f</math> and any formal sum of monomials <math>A=a_1+a_2+\cdots</math>, the ''plethystic substitution'' f[A] is the formal series obtained by making the substitutions

: <math>p_k \longrightarrow a_1^k+a_2^k+a_3^k+\cdots</math>

in the decomposition of <math>f</math> as a polynomial in the ''p''<sub>k</sub>'s.

==Examples==

If <math>X</math> denotes the formal sum <math>X=x_1+x_2+\cdots</math>, then <math>f[X]=f(x_1,x_2,\ldots)</math>.

One can write <math>1/(1-t)</math> to denote the formal sum <math>1+t+t^2+t^3+\cdots</math>, and so the plethystic substitution <math>f[1/(1-t)]</math> is simply the result of setting <math>x_i=t^{i-1}</math> for each i.  That is,

: <math>f\left[\frac{1}{1-t}\right]=f(1,t,t^2,t^3,\ldots)</math>.

Plethystic substitution can also be used to change the number of variables: if <math>X=x_1+x_2+\cdots + x_n</math>, then <math>f[X]=f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)</math> is the corresponding symmetric function in the ring <math>\Lambda_R(x_1,\ldots,x_n)</math> of symmetric functions in ''n'' variables.

Several other common substitutions are listed below.  In all of the following examples, <math>X=x_1+x_2+\cdots</math> and <math>Y=y_1+y_2+\cdots</math> are formal sums.

*If <math>f</math> is a homogeneous symmetric function of degree <math>d</math>, then
*: <math>f[tX]=t^d f(x_1,x_2,\ldots)</math>
*If <math>f</math> is a homogeneous symmetric function of degree <math>d</math>, then 
*: <math>f[-X]=(-1)^d \omega f(x_1,x_2,\ldots)</math>, 
: where <math>\omega</math> is the well-known involution on symmetric functions that sends a [[Schur polynomial|Schur function]] <math>s_{\lambda}</math> to the conjugate Schur function <math>s_{\lambda^\ast}</math>.
*The substitution <math>S:f\mapsto f[-X]</math> is the antipode for the [[Hopf algebra]] structure on the [[Ring of symmetric functions]].
*<math>p_n[X+Y]=p_n[X]+p_n[Y]</math>
*The map <math>\Delta: f\mapsto f[X+Y]</math> is the coproduct for the Hopf algebra structure on the ring of symmetric functions.
*<math>h_n\left[X(1-t)\right]</math> is the alternating Frobenius series for the [[exterior algebra]] of the defining representation of the [[symmetric group]], where <math>h_n</math> denotes the complete homogeneous symmetric function of degree <math>n</math>.
*<math>h_n\left[X/(1-t)\right]</math> is the Frobenius series for the [[symmetric algebra]] of the defining representation of the symmetric group.
